summary: This resolution sets floor procedures for House consideration of four bills (S. 1383 on a Veterans Advisory Committee, H.R. 2189 on firearms modernization, H.R. 261 on undersea cables in marine sanctuaries, and H.R. 3617 on critical energy resources) by waiving points of order, adopting specified substitute amendments, limiting debate to one hour, and waiving the two-thirds vote requirement for certain rules reports through February 13, 2026.

scores.thoughts: The resolution includes a procedural waiver for continuing appropriations resolutions but does not authorize, increase, or decrease any spending. This is purely procedural and has no substantive bearing on government spending levels.
None of the four underlying bills or the procedural provisions address tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
The Veterans Advisory Committee bill touches veterans' issues but does not engage healthcare policy, coverage, or delivery systems.

Section 2 sets up floor consideration of H.R. 2189, which directly modernizes federal firearms laws for new technology and less-than-lethal weapons. This engages the topic, and the framing suggests updating rules to accommodate rather than restrict new options, producing a moderate positive effect.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or pathways for legal status.
No provisions address reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or national security spending.

Section 3 sets up consideration of H.R. 261, which limits additional federal authorizations required for undersea fiber optic cables inside national marine sanctuaries. This reduces regulatory hurdles in protected marine areas and therefore has a modest positive (deregulatory) effect on the topic.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related entitlements.
No provisions address schools, federal education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The minor appropriations waiver does not alter deficit levels or debt-reduction priorities.
The Veterans Advisory Committee on Equal Access does not expand or restrict legal protections on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
No provisions address religious exemptions or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
